To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a dynamic pooling operator can be used to adaptively select the pooling regions for the detection of complex events, and that a globally optimal inference algorithm can be used to efficiently implement the dynamic pooling.

1) a dynamic pooling operator can be defined to enable a unified treatment of video event segmentation, temporal structure, and event classification, 2) a large margin classifier with latent variables can be used to efficiently infer the most informative segment locations for each sequence, and 3) the resulting event detector outperforms existing methods.

a) the problem of adaptively choosing the regions for pooling can be cast as the inference problem of a large-margin classifier with latent variables; and b) the resulting dynamic pooling approach is a powerful framework for the classification of videos with complex events.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of detecting and classifying complex events in video, which is a key problem in many applications, such as video indexing and retrieval.
the problem of adaptively determining the regions to pool in order to detect a given event in video.
developing new models and techniques for complex event detection, which are based on dynamic pooling of spatiotemporal information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method provides a unified framework for the detection of complex events in video.
the paper presents a novel approach for event detection that can adapt to changes in the event temporal configuration and can handle complex events composed of multiple characteristic behaviors.
the paper proposes a method to detect complex events in video, and it does so with state-of-the-art results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, by combining a novel pooling operator with a large-margin classifier with latent variables, we are able to achieve a unified solution to event specific video segmentation and temporal structure modeling, as well as event detection.
we have shown that it is possible to learn a complex event detector from a few examples, by jointly learning a model of video structure and a model of the event.
we have developed a novel approach to complex event detection that is based on dynamic pooling of features extracted from segments of a video.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of event-specific video segmentation can be addressed by modeling it as an inference problem over the locations of segments.

, by treating video as an instance of a probabilistic model, it is possible to design an event detector that can adaptively learn the best video representation for each event, from a large family of pooling operators.
, by dynamically selecting the regions of the video that are most informative for event detection, it is possible to achieve a substantial performance boost.
